clue.text: Pop's shelter sheltering ultimate unit

indicators.note: one shelter covering another word means its letters wrap around that word

parts.note: a lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a monad is a philosophical ultimate, indivisible unit

explanation.surface: A dad's hideout protects some final element of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop's' reads as a father's, but Pop is the fizzy drink and the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a colloquial name for a fizzy soft drink, and this lemon drink is one.

clue.text: River interrupting capital growth

indicators.note: breaking into the middle of another word, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A river flows through a capital city, spurring its expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatty benign tumour is a kind of growth on the body.

clue.text: Soldier encountering resistance in state

indicators.note: resistance is placed in the state, so its letter sits inside the state's name

parts.note: Maine is a US state
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A soldier meets opposition somewhere in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the marine corps is a sea-going soldier.

clue.text: Indicate how to play number to gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Showing how to perform a musical number for an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To write music down in notation is to show a performer how to play it.

clue.text: Losing volume of stupid smutty jokes, reportedly

indicators.note: says the phrase is heard rather than spelt, as if passed on by word of mouth

parts.note: stupid gives DIM, smutty jokes give INNUENDO, together DIM INNUENDO

explanation.surface: Dim-witted dirty jokes are said to be getting quieter.
explanation.walkthrough: DIM INNUENDO said quickly sounds like the musical term; the doubled N disappears in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the term marks a gradual decrease in loudness, a passage losing volume.

clue.text: Thrashes depilatory treatment soundly?

indicators.note: the question mark flags that 'soundly' means as heard, not thoroughly

parts.note: waxing removes hair, so wax is a depilatory treatment

explanation.surface: Someone gives a thorough beating to a hair-removal session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like it goes with 'Thrashes' (beats thoroughly), but it signals a word heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean hits hard and repeatedly, beats as a punishment.

clue.text: Revised maths with nun, one into bloodsports

indicators.note: revised means reworked, so the letters of maths and nun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun has gone over her maths, alongside someone fond of hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who follows the hounds on a fox hunt is someone keen on bloodsports.

clue.text: Minister to bloke getting stretched out

parts.note: chap and bloke are both informal words for a man
lain is the past participle of lie, to be stretched out

explanation.surface: A minister ministers to a man who is lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a chapel, college or regiment is a minister of religion.

clue.text: Rejoice about 11 getting drunk

indicators.note: one word goes round another, so its letters wrap around the second

parts.note: to sing is to rejoice in song
eleven players make a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: Celebrating as a team of eleven gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to 11 across, but it is just the number eleven, a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is British slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Shave, holding glove back, on and off

indicators.note: one word holds another, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: to pare is to shave or trim thinly

indicators.note: the word for glove is read backwards

parts.note: a mitt is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: Shaving while wearing a glove backwards, on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: Working only some of the time is doing it intermittently, on and off.

clue.text: Had grub after pub — that's natural

indicators.note: the eating comes after the pub, so its letters follow

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ate means had food, grub being slang for food

explanation.surface: Eating after a visit to the pub is only natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn qualities are natural ones, present from birth.

clue.text: Nothing's out of order in compiler's uninspiring delivery

indicators.note: the two pieces go in the setter's word, so they sit inside it

parts.note: the compiler of the crossword refers to himself as me
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
not on is a British idiom for unacceptable, out of order

explanation.surface: Nothing is wrong with the setter's flat, dull way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' looks like an anagram signal but is the idiom NOT ON; O and NOT ON go inside ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery all on one pitch is dull and flat, an uninspiring way of speaking.

clue.text: Refuge for some greasy lumberjacks

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A place of shelter for a few oily tree-fellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Political sanctuary is a refuge offered to those fleeing persecution.

clue.text: Couscous with HP sauce? Magic!

indicators.note: a sauce is a mix poured over, so these letters are mixed up; HP is a famous British brown sauce

explanation.surface: Couscous served with HP brown sauce, a wonderful combination!
explanation.walkthrough: HP Sauce is a well-known British brown sauce brand, which makes 'sauce' work in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conjuror's incantation, so it stands for magic or trickery.

clue.text: Disparagement of toad in trouble, holding blood and guts back

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the other piece inside them
trouble means stirred up, so the letters of toad and in are thrown into disorder
the word for blood and guts is read backwards

parts.note: gore is spilt blood and guts

explanation.surface: A toad in difficulty is being belittled, with blood and guts on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' looks like a single phrase about the toad, but 'in' is part of the fodder and 'trouble' alone signals the jumble; 'back' and 'holding' then work on the gore.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks belittle someone, so this noun means belittlement or disparagement.

clue.text: Gondoliers maybe reshaping a treetop

indicators.note: reshaping means forming anew, so these letters are given a new order

explanation.surface: Venetian boatmen are perhaps pruning the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gondoliers is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, so 'Gondoliers' is an example, not boatmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers is an example of a light comic opera.

clue.text: Necessarily involves devouring last of father's guts

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: to entail is to involve as a necessary consequence

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word father is taken

explanation.surface: Something inevitably requires eating a father's innards.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestines and inner organs are an animal's guts.

clue.text: Man introducing students and soldier to sex worker

indicators.note: the man brings the others in, so they go inside his name

parts.note: Carl is a man's name
L is a learner driver's plate, doubled for students
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A man introduces some students and a soldier to a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A prostitute who takes bookings by phone is a sex worker.

clue.text: God given month to beat VIP

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
Jan is short for January
to drum is to beat

explanation.surface: A god is given a month to defeat an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a mock-grand title for a self-important bigwig, a VIP.

clue.text: Fairy King getting hot

parts.note: Elvis Presley is known as the King of rock and roll
H is the abbreviation for hot on a tap

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale king gets steamy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin or relating to elves, so an adjective meaning like a fairy.

clue.text: Washed-out friend taking cover

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a lid covers a pot

explanation.surface: A tired-looking friend takes shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale, colourless face looks washed-out.

clue.text: Container for egos with upper half lowered

indicators.note: in a down clue the top three letters of the word are taken to the bottom

parts.note: egos are selves, one's sense of self

explanation.surface: A box for one's egos with its top half pushed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug, bowl or barrel is a vessel, something that holds liquid.

clue.text: Early bird's third to be stirred? Not often

indicators.note: only the third letter of the word bird is used
stirring mixes things up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An early bird is a third of the way to waking up, which seldom happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done seldom is done not often.

clue.text: Liquid lost through skinhead's aggressive behaviour

parts.note: the head of the word skin is its first letter
pillage is violent plundering

explanation.surface: Drink is spilt because of a thug's violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' looks like a shaven-headed yob, but read as skin's head it is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: When liquid is spilt and lost, the loss is a spill.

clue.text: Matters that don't?

parts.note: read as things that don't matter: unimportant details

explanation.surface: A riddle about subjects that do not matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matters' first reads as a noun, then the verb sense finishes it: matters that don't matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty details of no importance are matters that do not count.

clue.text: Experts concealing mound from Greek hero

indicators.note: hiding one thing inside another, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: aces are experts
a hill is a mound

explanation.surface: Experts are hiding a mound of earth from a Greek warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The great warrior of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad is a hero of Greek myth.

clue.text: Saint's solution to tree

parts.note: ans. is the abbreviation for answer, a solution
an elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A holy man's answer to a tree problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Anselm of Canterbury was an archbishop and canonised saint.

clue.text: Bloomer: unfortunate lapse involving builder's tool

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the other piece inside them
unfortunate means gone wrong, so the letters of lapse are put in a new order

parts.note: a hod carries bricks for a builder

explanation.surface: A blunder: a sorry slip with a builder's equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, matching 'lapse', but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a plant that flowers, and this lily-like plant does.
